summary: Iteration 38: tested the security audit fixes and the AI Work Order feature, backend (pytest, 9 tests) and frontend (Playwright, logged in as SuperAdmin). Backend: 8/9 pass. POST /api/ai/wo-terms returns 401 without a token. With a token it returns a detailed English scopeOfWork and 10-15 numbered aiTerms in about 20s. The AI terms cover safety, labour law, insurance and measurement, and do not repeat the payment/delivery/penalty/warranty/GST defaults. Logout invalidates the token (401). force_logout invalidates the target user's token (401). After 5 wrong passwords, the 6th attempt returns 429, even with the correct password. DELETE /api/fooding by a non-admin returns 403. SEC-004 same-step lock works: on approved paybills and bills, a User-role amount change gets 403, a remarks/utrNo change gets 200, and an approver can still change amounts. FAILED: a step-demotion bypass (details in critical issues). Frontend: wo-btn-ai is the next element after wo-btn-approve. With no item description, clicking it shows the toast 'Pehle line items add karein' and no modal opens. With items filled, the label shows 'AI likh raha hai…' and the modal opens in about 20s with editable English text in wo-ai-scope and wo-ai-terms. Save closes the modal, and reopening shows the saved, edited text without regenerating. Export opens a print window with 'A-1. Detailed Scope of Work', 'C. Terms & Conditions' (company defaults) and 'D. Additional Terms & Conditions' (AI text) as separate sections. SEC-001: the inline Reports Hub table, expanded row and biodata show '' and '

critical.issue: SEC-004 bypass. The financial-field lock only applies when new_step == old_step and old_step >= 3. A non-approver (role User) can send step:1 together with a changed amount on an approved (step 3) bill. The server returns 200 and stores step=1, basicAmount=777777. Approved records can be silently demoted and altered, and the existing approvedByName is also kept. Reproduced in test_step_demotion_bypass.

minor.issue: The rate limit is keyed only on identifier and stored in process memory. Anyone can lock the SuperAdmin out for 15 minutes with 5 bad attempts, there is no per-IP limit, and the counter resets when the server restarts.

Session invalidation is per user, not per token. A token issued before logout becomes valid again once the user logs in again from any device, because current_session.active flips back to true. Consider adding a session id (sid) claim to the JWT and comparing it with current_session.sid.

The regex is broad. Substrings like 'net' and 'rate' also match non-financial keys such as 'generatedAt' and 'internetNo'. A non-approver editing an approved record that has such client-side keys could get an unexpected 403. Consider anchoring the regex or using an explicit field list.
